entities.summary:
Guillaume de Nangis, also known as William of Nangis, was a French chronicler born in the 13th century, whose life and works spanned the tumultuous period of the Late Middle Ages. His most notable achievement was the compilation of the Chronica Majora, a vast and detailed history of the world from creation to the year 1307, which covered the entire medieval period, including the Crusades, the rise of the Mongols, and the reign of the Holy Roman Empire.

As a chronicler, de Nangis played a significant role in shaping the historical narrative of the medieval period, providing a unique perspective on the events and figures of the time. His work also served as a source of inspiration for later historians, such as the French historian Jean Froissart, who relied heavily on de Nangis's chronicle for his own accounts of the period.

Despite his significant contributions to the field of medieval history, de Nangis's life and work have largely been overshadowed by the more famous chroniclers of the time, such as William of Newburgh and Matthew Paris. Nevertheless, his Chronica Majora remains an important and valuable source of information on the medieval period, providing a detailed and nuanced understanding of the events and figures that shaped the world of the 13th century.

The Chronica Majora, de Nangis's magnum opus, is a testament to his skill as a historian and his ability to weave together a complex tapestry of events and stories. Its sheer size and scope make it a remarkable achievement, covering over 2,000 years of history and including accounts of the lives and reigns of numerous kings, queens, and nobles.
